steps.title: Prepare dissection area
steps.instruction: Clean the dissection box with 10 % bleach (10 min contact) then with freshly prepared 70 % ethanol; place the box on absorbent pads. Label a −80 °C box for 1.5 mL nuclease‑free LoBind tubes (Eppendorf catalog 022431021) and keep it on dry ice. Pre‑chill all 1.5 mL tubes, nuclease‑free spatula, petri dishes and toothed forceps on dry ice.

steps.title: Dissect frozen brain tissue
steps.instruction: Fill the dissection box with dry ice, cover the surface completely and wait 15–20 min for the chamber to equilibrate. Add 50–100 mg Drierite (8 mesh) to absorb moisture. On a pre‑chilled petri dish, dissect each sample (≈0.5 cm piece) to obtain 50 ± 5 mg tissue, weigh quickly in a pre‑chilled 1.5 mL tube, and immediately return the tube to dry ice and then to the −80 °C storage box. Wipe spatula and forceps with 70 % ethanol and discard the petri dish in a biohazard bin. Clean the box again the next morning with 10 % bleach (10 min) then 70 % ethanol. Store tissue at −80 °C or proceed to nuclei isolation.

steps.title: Prepare isolation buffers
steps.instruction: Make all buffers fresh, keep on wet ice, and use within 6 h (360 min).

substeps.instruction: Wash Buffer (1 ×, 8 mL for 4 samples): 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 % BSA, 0.1 % Tween‑20, bring to 8 mL with nuclease‑free water; store on ice (≤6 h).

1 × Lysis Buffer (2 mL total, 200 µL needed per 4 samples): 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 % Tween‑20, 0.1 % Nonidet P40, 0.01 % Digitonin (incubate at 65 °C to dissolve precipitate), 1 % BSA, bring to 2 mL with nuclease‑free water; keep on ice (≤6 h).
Lysis Dilution Buffer (2 mL for 4 samples): 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, 1 % BSA, bring to 2 mL with nuclease‑free water; keep on ice (≤6 h).
0.1 × Lysis Buffer (200 µL for 4 samples): mix 200 µL 1 × Lysis Buffer with 1.8 mL Lysis Dilution Buffer (final 0.1 ×). Keep on ice.
Sucrose Cushion Buffer I (12 mL for 4 samples): 10.8 mL Nuclei PURE 2 M sucrose solution (4 °C) + 1.2 mL Nuclei PURE sucrose cushion buffer (4 °C); keep on ice.
Diluted Nuclei Buffer (2 mL for ≈4 samples): 100 µL Nuclei Buffer 20× (−20 °C) + 1.9 mL nuclease‑free water; keep on ice (use within 1 h).

steps.title: Set up centrifuge and reagents
steps.instruction: Set centrifuge temperature to 4 °C. Mark all 1.5 mL and 15 mL tubes. Thaw or equilibrate all reagents to room temperature (20–25 °C) unless a specific temperature is required (e.g., digitonin at 65 °C).

steps.title: Lyse tissue and release nuclei
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL chilled 0.1 × Lysis Buffer to each frozen tissue tube, homogenize 15 times with a pellet pestle (Fisherbrand™ Pellet Pestle™ Cordless Motor, catalog 12‑141‑364). Incubate on ice 5 min, pipette‑mix 10 times, incubate on ice another 10 min.

steps.title: Wash nuclei
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL chilled Wash Buffer, pipette‑mix 5–7 times, then pass the suspension through a pre‑wet 70 µm cell strainer (wet with 1 × PBS) into a precooled 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Sucrose cushion and gradient
steps.instruction: Add 1.8 mL Sucrose Cushion Buffer I to the 15 mL tube, mix 10 times. Prepare two 2 mL tubes each containing 500 µL Sucrose Cushion Buffer I. Divide the 2.8 mL nuclei suspension equally (1.4 mL each) and layer gently on top of the 500 µL cushion in each tube. Centrifuge at 13 000 g for 45 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove myelin and resuspend nuclei
steps.instruction: Inspect the top of each tube for a white sticky myelin layer; remove it carefully with a 1 mL pipette tip or sterile spatula without disturbing the pellet. Remove supernatant leaving 100 µL, resuspend the pellet by gentle pipetting (~10 times). Add 500 µL Wash Buffer, pipette‑mix 8–10 times until nuclei are fully resuspended.

steps.title: Final filtration and counting
steps.instruction: Pass the resuspended nuclei through a 40 µm Flowmi cell strainer into a new 1.5 mL tube. Combine the two 1.5 mL aliquots (total ≈1.2 mL). Take 10 µL of the suspension, add 1 µL DAPI (or trypan blue) and count nuclei with a cell counter. Centrifuge the tube at 500 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in chilled Diluted Nuclei Buffer using the concentration table supplied with the Chromium Next GEM ATAC kit.

steps.title: Dilute nuclei to loading concentration
steps.instruction: Calculate the volume of Nuclei Stock to load 10 000–15 000 nuclei per Chromium chip (total volume 5 µL). Use the formula: Volume (Nuclei Stock µL) = (Targeted Nuclei Recovery × 1.53) / (Nuclei Stock conc nuclei/µL). Then add Diluted Nuclei Buffer to bring the final volume to 5 µL. Verify the calculation (≈5 min).

steps.title: Transposition reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare Transposition Mix according to the Chromium Next GEM Single Cell ATAC Reagent Kit v1/v1.1 manual. Add the calculated volume of diluted nuclei to the mix, pipette‑mix gently, and incubate in a thermal cycler for the time and temperature specified in the kit (≈70–80 min).

steps.title: GEM generation and barcoding
steps.instruction: Prepare the Master Mix as described in the kit. Load Chromium Next GEM Chip H with (i) Master Mix and transposed nuclei in row 1, (ii) Gel Beads in row 2, (iii) Partitioning Oil in row 3. Run the chip on the Chromium Controller, transfer GEMs to a tube strip, and incubate in a thermal cycler for the kit‑specified cycling (≈1.5 h). Store GEMs at 15 °C for up to 18 h or at −20 °C for up to 1 week if needed.

steps.title: Post‑GEM cleanup
steps.instruction: Add the Recovery Agent to each sample (do not pipette‑mix). Remove and discard the pink Recovery Agent/oil phase. Add Dynabeads Cleanup Mix, incubate as per kit instructions, capture on a magnetic separator, and perform two washes with freshly prepared 80 % ethanol. Add Elution Solution, incubate for the time indicated, capture on magnet, and transfer supernatant. Add SPRIselect reagent, incubate, capture, wash twice with 80 % ethanol, elute with Elution Solution, and capture again. Store cleaned library at 4 °C (≤72 h) or −20 °C (≤2 weeks). (≈50 min).

steps.title: Library construction (PCR)
steps.instruction: Prepare Sample Index PCR Mix per the kit, add to each sample, and add the appropriate Single Index primer. Run PCR in a thermal cycler using the cycling conditions in the kit (≈2 h). After PCR, add SPRIselect reagent, incubate 5 min, capture on magnet, wash twice with 80 % ethanol, elute with Buffer EB, mix, and incubate as instructed. Transfer the final eluate to a new strip tube.

steps.title: Library QC and normalization
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with Qubit (ng/µL) and fragment size with Agilent TapeStation High Sensitivity D1000 or Bioanalyzer HS DNA chip. Convert ng/µL to nM using: nM = (ng/µL × 10⁶) / (660 g/mol × average library size bp). Normalize each library to the concentration required for pooling (e.g., 300 nM for NovaSeq). Prepare a sheet with sample name, ng/µL, average size (bp), calculated nM, volume of library needed for 50 nM, and water volume to reach 20 µL total. Pool libraries and dilute to the final loading concentration for the sequencer.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the pooled library onto a compatible Illumina instrument (e.g., NovaSeq 6000 S4) using paired‑end, dual‑index 150 bp reads. Follow the instrument manual for loading concentration (typically 300 nM) and run parameters. Sequencing takes ~2 working days.

steps.title: Install cellranger‑atac and reference
steps.instruction: Download cellranger‑atac v2.0.0 from 10× Genomics and install on a Linux PC or HPC cluster. Download the human reference archive refdata‑cellranger‑arc‑GRCh38‑2020‑A‑2.0.0.tar.gz, then unzip with: `tar -xvf refdata-cellranger-arc-GRCh38-2020-A-2.0.0.tar.gz`.

steps.title: Generate accessibility matrix with cellranger‑atac
steps.instruction: Create variables: `Input_path='Your_Fastq_Input_path/'`, `Output_path='Your_Project_Output_path/cellranger_atac_output/'`, `annotation='Your_atac_annotation_Path/refdata-cellranger-arc-GRCh38-2020-A-2.0.0/'`. Run for each sample: `cellranger-atac count --id=$Output_path/Your_Sample --reference=$annotation --fastqs=$Input_path --sample=$Your_Sample_Name --localcores=32 --localmem=128` (≈2–3 h per sample).

steps.title: Create ArrowFiles and ArchRProject
steps.instruction: In R (v4.1.1) load ArchR, then: `cellranger_dir='Path_to_cellranger/cellranger_atac_output'`; `sample_names=dir(cellranger_dir)[grepl('Sample',dir(cellranger_dir))]`; `sample_files=paste0(cellranger_dir,'/',sample_names,'/outs/fragments.tsv.gz')`. Create ArrowFiles with `createArrowFiles(inputFiles=sample_files, sampleNames=sample_names, filterTSS=4, filterFrags=1000, addTileMat=TRUE)` (≈20–30 min per sample). Build an ArchRProject: `proj1 <- ArchRProject(ArrowFiles=arrowFiles, outputDirectory='ArchR_Project')`.

steps.title: Quality control and doublet removal
steps.instruction: Infer doublets: `proj1 <- addDoubletScores(proj1)`. Filter nuclei: `proj1 <- filterDoublets(proj1, filterRatio=1)`. Optionally filter by fragment count (`proj1$nFrags > 3000`).

steps.title: Batch correction, clustering and UMAP
steps.instruction: Add Harmony batch correction: `proj1 <- addHarmony(proj1, groupBy='Batch')`. Perform dimensionality reduction and clustering: `proj1 <- addIterativeLSI(proj1); proj1 <- addClusters(proj1, resolution=0.8); proj1 <- addUMAP(proj1, reducedDims='IterativeLSI')` (≈2.5 h).

steps.title: Pseudo‑bulk replicates and peak calling
steps.instruction: Group nuclei by cluster and create pseudo‑bulk replicates: `proj1 <- addGroupCoverages(proj1, groupBy='Clusters')`. Call peaks with MACS2 (v2.2.7.1) via ArchR: `proj1 <- addReproduciblePeakSet(proj1, pathToMacs2='$(which macs2)')` (≈2.5 h).

steps.title: Install and load ArchRtoSignac
steps.instruction: In R, run: `if(!require(devtools)) install.packages('devtools')`; `devtools::install_github('swaruplabUCI/ArchRtoSignac')`; `library(ArchRtoSignac)`; also load required packages: `library(ArchR); library(Signac); library(Seurat); library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86)` (≈20–30 min).

steps.title: Convert ArchRProject to Signac SeuratObject
steps.instruction: Run the conversion wrapper: `seurat_atac <- ArchRtoSignac::ArchR2Signac(ArchRProject=proj1, fragments_dir='Path_to_cellranger_atac_output', reference='EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86', seqStyle='UCSC', refversion='hg38')`. Verify conversion with `all.equal(colnames(seurat_atac), gsub('#','_',rownames(proj1@cellColData)))` (should return TRUE).

steps.title: Add dimension reduction to SeuratObject
steps.instruction: Transfer Harmony/IterativeLSI embeddings and UMAP from ArchR to the Seurat object using `addDimRed(seurat_atac, reducedDims='Harmony')`. The UMAP embedding will be added automatically.

steps.title: Signac cell‑type identification (reference mapping)
steps.instruction: Load a reference scRNA‑seq dataset (e.g., from Liger integration). Switch Seurat default assay to RNA: `DefaultAssay(seurat_atac) <- 'RNA'`. Find anchors: `anchors <- FindTransferAnchors(reference=seurat_reference, query=seurat_atac, reduction='cca')`. Map query to reference: `seurat_atac <- MapQuery(anchorset=anchors, query=seurat_atac, reference=seurat_reference, refdata=list(celltype='celltype'), reference.reduction='lsi')`. Adjust `predicted.cluster.score` cutoff (e.g., ≥0.90) and filter low‑score nuclei (`seurat_atac <- subset(seurat_atac, predicted.cluster.score >= 0.90)`). (≈100 min).

steps.title: Differential accessibility analysis
steps.instruction: Set assay to peaks: `DefaultAssay(seurat_atac) <- 'peaks'`. Identify differentially accessible peaks between groups with `da_peaks <- FindMarkers(seurat_atac, ident.1='GroupA', ident.2='GroupB', min.pct=0.1, test.use='LR')`. Perform motif enrichment (`enriched.motifs <- FindMotifs(seurat_atac, features=da_peaks)`) and TF footprinting (`Footprint(seurat_atac, motif='TF_name')`). Use rGREAT for genomic region enrichment: `library(rGREAT); job <- submitGreatJob(bed=da_peaks, species='hg38')`.

steps.title: Optional advanced analyses
steps.instruction: Run additional downstream analyses such as trajectory inference with Monocle3, co‑accessibility with Cicero, or integration with scRNA‑seq using Seurat wrappers. These steps typically require 4–5 working days depending on dataset size.

description: Assay for transposase-accessible chromatin coupled with high-throughput sequencing (ATAC-seq) is a simple, fast, and sensitive method for mapping chromatin accessibility genome-wide and is therefore considered as an alternative to other methods like DNase-seq or MNase-seq (Buenrostro et al., 2015). ATAC-seq works well across many cell types and species and requires only 50,000 cells or less to capture regulatory elements (Shashikant and Ettensohn, 2019). However, bulk measurements of chromatin accessibility limit the precise understanding of how specific cell-types contribute to overall disease etiology (Fang et al., 2021). Recent innovations in single-cell genomics have enabled scalable profiling of chromatin with cellular or subcellular resolution using single nucleus ATAC-seq (snATAC-seq) (Rai et al., 2020; Ziffra et al., 2021). The typical bulk ATAC or snATAC-seq protocol requires nuclei extracted from fresh cells and tissues, due to the significant disruptive effect of freezing on chromatin integrity and structure. However, intensive effort has been made to introduce modifications in the snATAC-seq protocol to allow nuclei extraction from frozen tissues, including frozen mammalian brains. The current protocol provides a simple yet highly reproducible pipeline for isolation of single nuclei from frozen postmortem human brains followed by library preparation for snATAC-seq and downstream bioinformatics analysis. The tissue dissection protocol and modified single nucleus isolation protocol together give rise to enough intact nuclei from the frozen brain to achieve targeted nuclei recovery for further processing. Additionally, our integrated bioinformatic protocol using both ArchR and Signac pipelines (Granja et al., 2021; Stuart et al., 2021) provides an approach, specifically an R package (ArchRtoSignac), to convert an ArchRProject to a Signac SeuratObject. This conversion R package keeps the 501 bp fixed-width open chromatin regions in the peak matrix generated
